# teams app get

Get a Teams app

## Usage

```
teams app get [appId] [options]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `appId` | App ID | No |

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--json` | [OPTIONAL] Output as JSON |
| `--web` | [OPTIONAL] Print the install and Developer Portal links |
| `--install-link` | [OPTIONAL] Print just the install link (pipe-friendly) |
<!-- AUTOGENERATED:END -->

## Details

Displays detailed information about a Teams app.

### Messaging Mode

For both Teams-managed and Azure bots, the human-readable output shows the configured messaging mode. Use the `socketMode` field in JSON to inspect it programmatically. This reads the bot registration; it does not verify that your running application has connected.

```bash
teams app get <appId> --json
```

After changing modes with [app update](./update#messaging-mode), restart your Teams SDK application. Use [app doctor](./doctor) to check the bot configuration.

### JSON Output

Use `--json` to output app details for scripting:

```bash
teams app get <appId> --json
```

Available fields: `appId`, `teamsAppId`, `name`, `longName`, `version`, `developer`, `shortDescription`, `longDescription`, `websiteUrl`, `privacyUrl`, `termsOfUseUrl`, `endpoint`, `socketMode`, `installLink`, `portalLink`.

`socketMode` is always included: `true` for sockets, `false` for HTTP (including bots without a communication configuration), or `null` when there is no bot or the mode could not be read.

### Install Link

Get the Teams install deep link:

```bash
teams app get <appId> --web
```

### Interactive Mode

Without `[appId]`, launches a searchable app picker that loops — view one app, then pick another or exit.
